Compare the overall scar patterns of groups of cores

Source: R/group_tests.R
compare_groups.Rd

Tests whether groups of cores differ in their scar patterns as a whole, using a set of features such as those of spharm_spatiodirection(). Three permutation tests on Euclidean distances are reported side by side, for all groups together and for every pair of groups:

Usage

compare_groups(
  x,
  group,
  features = NULL,
  permutations = 999,
  alpha = 0.05,
  p_adjust = "holm",
  permdisp_type = c("centroid", "median"),
  seed = 2226
)

Arguments

x

A data frame or numeric matrix with one row per core, such as the output of spharm_spatiodirection().

group

The groups: the name of a column of x, or a vector with one value per row of x.

features

Names of the columns of x to compare. Default: the features recorded by spharm_spatiodirection() (attribute "features"), else the columns named like its features (dir_1, start_2, ...), else all numeric columns except n_scar.

permutations

Number of permutations of each test. Default 999.

alpha

Significance level used for the notes. Default 0.05.

p_adjust

Method for adjusting the pairwise p values within each test, passed to stats::p.adjust(). Default "holm".

permdisp_type

Distances to the group "centroid" (default, the original PERMDISP) or to the spatial "median"; passed to vegan::betadisper().

seed

Seed set before each test, so each is reproducible on its own; the caller's random stream is restored afterwards. NULL uses the current stream. Default 2226.

Value

An object of class spharmlithic_group_comparison, a list with

overall

A tibble with one row per test: test, statistic (pseudo-F for PERMANOVA and PERMDISP, \(W_d^*\)), R2 (PERMANOVA) and p.

pairwise

With three or more groups, a tibble with one row per pair: group1, group2, n1, n2, the statistic and p value of each test, the adjusted p values (*_p_adj) and note; NULL with two groups.

groups

The number of cores per group.

features

The columns compared.

settings

The arguments used.

Printing the object shows both tables and the notes.

Details

  • PERMANOVA (Anderson 2001): do the group centroids differ?

  • PERMDISP (Anderson 2006): do the groups differ in dispersion, the spread of their cores around their centroid?

  • the \(W_d^*\) test (Hamidi et al. 2019): a Welch-type test of the centroids that allows the groups to differ in dispersion.

When PERMDISP is significant, PERMANOVA may mistake a difference in dispersion for a difference in location, especially with unequal group sizes; the location difference should then be judged by \(W_d^*\). The printed result points out where this applies.

Rows with a missing feature or group are left out, and so are groups with fewer than two cores; a message says which. The features of spharm_spatiodirection() do not change with the scar count, so the scar count should not be added as a covariate.

The \(W_d^*\) statistic is computed in the package and agrees with WdStar::WdS() (Hamidi et al. 2019); its p value is the proportion of permutations of the group labels, the observed one included, with a statistic at least as large.

References

Anderson, M. J. (2001). A new method for non-parametric multivariate analysis of variance. Austral Ecology, 26(1), 32–46.

Anderson, M. J. (2006). Distance-based tests for homogeneity of multivariate dispersions. Biometrics, 62(1), 245–253.

Hamidi, B., Wallace, K., Vasu, C., & Alekseyenko, A. V. (2019). \(W_d^*\)-test: robust distance-based multivariate analysis of variance. Microbiome, 7, 51.

Holm, S. (1979). A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 6(2), 65–70.

See also

spharm_spatiodirection(), compare_indices(), pairwise_permanova()

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- data.frame(group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 8),
                f1 = rnorm(24, rep(c(0, 0, 1), each = 8)),
                f2 = rnorm(24, sd = rep(c(1, 3, 1), each = 8)))
compare_groups(x, "group", permutations = 199)
#> Group comparison of 2 features (Euclidean distance, 199 permutations)
#> Groups: A (n = 8), B (n = 8), C (n = 8) 
#> 
#> Overall
#>       test statistic     R2    p
#>  PERMANOVA     1.176 0.1007 0.35
#>   PERMDISP     4.358     NA 0.03
#>        W*d     2.017     NA 0.10
#> 
#> Pairwise (p values adjusted by holm within each test)
#>  group1 group2 n1 n2 PERMANOVA_p_adj PERMDISP_p_adj Wd_p_adj note
#>       A      B  8  8            0.99          0.105     1.00     
#>       A      C  8  8            0.15          0.865     0.09     
#>       B      C  8  8            0.46          0.105     0.44     
#> 
#> Note: PERMDISP is significant overall: the groups differ in dispersion,
#>       so PERMANOVA may confuse dispersion with location; judge the
#>       location difference by W*d.
